src/order/order.service.ts findOne(): ``throw new NotFoundException(`Order ${id} not found`);`` reports a missing order as an HTTP 404 exception (presentation/transport concern).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/order/order.service.ts is in the application layer but does transport/presentation work. Its findOne method accepts an Express Request object, so the service's contract depends on the HTTP framework. Both methods also report use-case outcomes with NestJS HTTP exceptions (BadRequestException, NotFoundException), which carry HTTP 400/404 status codes. Turning results into HTTP responses is the presentation layer's job (controllers or exception filters); the service should raise application or domain errors instead. The repository orchestration and the simple business checks are acceptable in an application service and were not counted as violations.

violations.message: findOne(id, request?: Request) takes the Express Request type in an application-layer service. Handling the HTTP request is presentation/transport work and belongs in the controller.

create() and findOne() throw NestJS HTTP exceptions (BadRequestException, NotFoundException), so the service reports outcomes as HTTP status codes. That is presentation/transport work; the service should raise application/domain errors and the controller or an exception filter should map them to HTTP responses.
